helpCenter.multiDevice.headline: Multi-device: every device is a Bakabase server
helpCenter.multiDevice.intro: Every device can run its own Bakabase: the all-in-one desktop app on a computer, or the server on a NAS or another host. Each manages its own storage and resources. You decide which devices may browse or manage it. Both desktop apps and headless servers can manage other devices.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.title: Three Bakabase servers on one local network, each with its own storage
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.caption.d: Its movies stay on its own drive. Once management is allowed, Resources → All devices can show and manage resources on the other devices.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.caption.l: Keeps the comics on its own disk. It can do everything the desktop PC can: every computer is an equal, not a client of another.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.caption.n: Its music stays here. Open its address in a browser to manage it. It can also add and manage other devices without a desktop window.
helpCenter.multiDevice.diagram.hint: Select a device to highlight its connections.
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.title: What every device has
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.server.des: The desktop app includes a complete Bakabase server; a NAS runs the same server in Docker.
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.storage.de: Media files stay on their owner. Managers sync resource metadata for local search; selected definitions can also sync between devices.
helpCenter.multiDevice.pillar.reach.desc: Desktop apps and servers can both manage devices that allow them to do so.
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.title: Resources and device management
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.browse.title: Unified resources
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.browse.desc: Use the normal resource list to search and manage local and managed resources, with device filters and source markers.
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.switch.title: Device management
helpCenter.multiDevice.ways.switch.desc: Add devices, manage access and map paths. Desktop apps can also open a managed device’s full interface in their window.
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.title: Side by side
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.see.brows: The normal resource list, filtered by device
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.see.switc: Device connections, permissions and path mappings
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.do.browse: Search locally; view and edit data on its owner
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.do.switch: Configure management connections and file access
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.play.brow: Browser or local app, according to file access and resource rules
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.play.swit: Path mappings make the same files accessible to local apps
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.access.br: An existing management connection to each selected device
helpCenter.multiDevice.compare.access.sw: Permission from the device being managed
helpCenter.multiDevice.trust: Each device decides who may manage it and can revoke access. Management grants no reverse or indirect access.
helpCenter.multiDevice.map.title: See how your devices connect
helpCenter.multiDevice.map.desc: The Device map shows management and data sync connections. Select a device or connection to inspect it, answer requests, revoke access or configure its path mappings.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.headline: Every device's library in one window
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.intro: The normal resource list includes this device and the devices it manages. Resource metadata syncs incrementally for local search, isolated by owner. Files remain on their owner.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.mock.capti: “This device” shows only what is on the computer you sit at.
“All devices” adds the laptop's comics and the NAS's music to the same list, each marked with the device it lives on.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.card.searc: Use the same resource filters, including device selection. Search runs on local metadata; remote changes appear after synchronization.
View and edit through the same interface. Writes go to the owner. Playback depends on file access, mappings and player capabilities.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.card.cover: Cached metadata remains searchable while a device is offline. File access and edits require the owner online; sync status shows whether metadata needs refreshing.
helpCenter.multiDevice.browse.boundary: Metadata management needs no path mappings. Local apps need a valid mapped path or a stream they support to open files.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.headline: Manage several devices in one place
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.intro: Desktop apps and headless servers can both be managers. Managed resources use the normal resource page and filters. Device management holds connections and mappings. The window switcher below is an additional desktop feature for opening a managed device’s full interface.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.mock.local: This computer's own library, settings and tasks.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.mock.remot: {{name}}'s library, settings and tasks. Changes made here happen on {{name}}.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.mock.capti: The window shows this computer. Pick another device in the list to switch to it.
The window shows {{name}}, and the switcher turns amber to say so. Pick this device at the top of the list to come back.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.play.title: Managing data and playing files are separate capabilities
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.play.capti: The viewing device keeps separate path mappings for each source. Local apps can open mapped files, while browsers and compatible players can use media streams from the source. Headless servers do not launch desktop players.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.card.ownUi: The window shows the interface that device ships with, so it always matches the version it runs.
helpCenter.multiDevice.switch.card.contr: Management permits changes to the other device’s data and settings. Only allow devices you trust. If A manages B, B does not automatically see A’s resources, and A does not inherit access to devices managed by B.
If a device runs an older version whose interface has no switcher, use “Switch to” in the tray icon's menu to come back.
Asks the device to revoke this computer, then deletes its key here. The device can also revoke this computer at any time.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.headline: Set it up on the Devices page
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.intro: Both desktop apps and servers have Devices under Multi-device. Open a server’s address in a browser to configure it. Access is granted on the device being accessed, separately for each pair.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.manage.allo: Allow it on the device to be managed
On its Devices page, under Management → Who may manage this device, turn on remote access (paired devices only). You can create a pairing code there too.
Add it on the managing device

Under Devices → Management → Add a device to manage, enter its address and pairing code. Without a code, request management and allow it on the other device. Desktop apps and headless servers both support this.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.manage.swit: Open Resources and select devices in the filter to search and manage their resources. Desktop apps can also open another device’s full interface in their window.
Under Management → Added devices → Path mappings, expand the source directory tree and choose its location here. Unsaved edits can be restored in the same browser.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.unrestricte: Docker servers default to Unrestricted, allowing network devices to access them without pairing. Bakabase shows a reminder. To change access, open the server’s address and adjust Configuration → Remote access.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.nas: Headless servers use the same management and data sync pages. Open their address in a browser to configure them.
helpCenter.multiDevice.setup.codes: Management pairing grants control of the device. Data sync codes grant access to selected definitions only; they do not grant management access.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.managemen: Full control of another device, granted on that device.

Desktop apps and headless servers can both manage devices. The normal Resources page searches local replicas of managed resource metadata; changes go to their owner. Device-wide settings remain on the owner’s page.
The managed device grants permission under Devices → Management. Create a pairing code there and enter it on the manager, or allow its request.
Management is one-way with no reverse or indirect access. Either device can end the connection.
Allowing a request shows the requesting device's name and address. Make sure it is the computer you expect before you allow it.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.pathMappi: Where another device's folders are, seen from the computer you sit at.

A mapping describes where the same files are accessible on the manager, usually through a previously mounted network share. Each managed device has separate mappings; no files are copied or moved.
Under Devices → Management → Added devices → Path mappings, expand the source directory tree and choose a local directory. The tree contains only that device’s own resources. Unsaved edits stay in this browser until restored, discarded or successfully saved. Review concurrent changes before replacing them.
Local apps use mapped files or supported streams. Metadata management does not require mappings.

The NAS keeps its music under /volume1/music, and this PC reaches the same folder as \\nas\music. With the mapping /volume1/music → \\nas\music, playing /volume1/music/Live/01.flac opens \\nas\music\Live\01.flac in this PC's player.
helpCenter.multiDevice.concept.remoteAcc: Which other devices a server answers, and what they may do.

Each server controls access through its remote access settings. Data sync access does not grant management rights.
Docker defaults to Unrestricted. Open the device’s address and adjust Configuration → Remote access to change this. Desktop apps can also open the managed device in their window.
Only use Unrestricted on a network where you trust every device: anyone who can reach it can delete files and change settings. Never expose Bakabase to the internet with port forwarding.
